title: Full Form MCQ — Part 1 (Simple)

UP Police training-bank topics are distinct from recruitment PYQs. Other questions are reference-based practice, not predictions.

questions.text: What is the full form of CPU?
questions.explanation: CPU: Central Processing Unit. The CPU executes program instructions.

questions.text: What is the full form of ALU?
questions.explanation: ALU: Arithmetic Logic Unit. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.

references.locator: Q22; wording normalized to standard terminology

questions.text: What is the full form of CU?
questions.explanation: CU: Control Unit. The control unit coordinates instruction execution.

questions.text: What is the full form of RAM?
questions.explanation: RAM: Random Access Memory. RAM holds working data; ordinary system RAM is volatile.

questions.text: What is the full form of ROM?
questions.explanation: ROM: Read Only Memory. ROM is nonvolatile storage associated with firmware.

questions.text: What is the full form of PROM?
questions.explanation: PROM: Programmable Read Only Memory. Classic PROM is programmed once after manufacture.

questions.text: What is the full form of EPROM?
questions.explanation: EPROM: Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. Classic EPROM can be erased using ultraviolet light.

questions.text: What is the full form of EEPROM?
options: Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
Electronic Extended Program Random Output Memory
Electrically Enabled Primary Read Only Memory
Erasable Electronic Permanent Random Open Memory
questions.explanation: EEPROM: Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. EEPROM can be erased and programmed electrically.

questions.text: What is the full form of SRAM?
questions.explanation: SRAM: Static Random Access Memory. SRAM is commonly used for caches and does not require periodic refresh while powered.

questions.text: What is the full form of DRAM?
questions.explanation: DRAM: Dynamic Random Access Memory. DRAM requires periodic refresh while powered.

questions.text: What is the full form of SDRAM?
questions.explanation: SDRAM: Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory. SDRAM synchronizes operations with a clock signal.

questions.text: What is the full form of DDR?
questions.explanation: DDR: Double Data Rate. DDR memory transfers data on both clock edges.

questions.text: What is the full form of DIMM?
questions.explanation: DIMM: Dual In-line Memory Module. A DIMM is a memory-module form factor.

questions.text: What is the full form of BIOS?
questions.explanation: BIOS: Basic Input Output System. BIOS initializes hardware during startup.

questions.text: What is the full form of ECC in computer memory?
questions.explanation: ECC: Error Correction Code. ECC uses redundancy to detect and correct certain data errors.

questions.text: What is the full form of NVRAM in computer memory?
questions.explanation: NVRAM: Nonvolatile Random Access Memory. NVRAM retains its stored contents when power is removed.

questions.text: What is the full form of POST?
questions.explanation: POST: Power On Self Test. POST checks hardware during startup.

questions.text: What is the full form of CMOS?
questions.explanation: CMOS: Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor. CMOS names a semiconductor technology, not an operating system.

questions.text: What is the full form of HDD?
questions.explanation: HDD: Hard Disk Drive. An HDD stores data on rotating magnetic platters.

questions.text: What is the full form of SSD?
questions.explanation: SSD: Solid State Drive. An SSD provides persistent storage without spinning platters.

questions.text: What is the full form of DMA?
questions.explanation: DMA: Direct Memory Access. DMA allows a device to transfer data to or from memory without CPU handling of every transfer.

questions.text: What is the full form of PCI?
questions.explanation: PCI: Peripheral Component Interconnect. PCI is a computer expansion-bus standard.

questions.text: What is the full form of SCSI?
questions.explanation: SCSI: Small Computer System Interface. SCSI defines interfaces and commands for connecting devices.

questions.text: What is the full form of RAID?
questions.explanation: RAID: Redundant Array of Independent Disks. RAID combines multiple drives. Older literature also uses “inexpensive”; both wordings are recognized, so that variant is not a distractor.

questions.text: What is the full form of UPS?
questions.explanation: UPS: Uninterruptible Power Supply. A UPS supplies temporary backup power during an outage.

questions.text: What is the full form of IC?
questions.explanation: IC: Integrated Circuit. An IC integrates electronic circuitry on a semiconductor chip.

questions.text: What is the full form of VLSI?
questions.explanation: VLSI: Very Large Scale Integration. VLSI refers to integrating very large numbers of components onto a chip.

questions.text: What is the full form of LSI?
questions.explanation: LSI: Large Scale Integration. LSI is a historical integrated-circuit complexity category.

questions.text: What is the full form of MSI?
questions.explanation: MSI: Medium Scale Integration. MSI is a historical integrated-circuit complexity category.

questions.text: What is the full form of SSI?
questions.explanation: SSI: Small Scale Integration. SSI is a historical integrated-circuit complexity category.

questions.text: What is the full form of OCR?
questions.explanation: OCR: Optical Character Recognition. OCR converts text in images into machine-readable characters.

questions.text: What is the full form of OMR for the technique used to detect filled bubbles on answer sheets?
questions.explanation: OMR: Optical Mark Recognition. OMR detects marked fields on forms. This question asks for the recognition technique; “Optical Mark Reader” names a device and is not used as a distractor.

questions.text: What is the full form of MICR for the cheque-reading technique?
questions.explanation: MICR: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition. MICR identifies characters printed using magnetic ink, commonly on bank cheques.

questions.text: What is the full form of LCD?
questions.explanation: LCD: Liquid Crystal Display. LCD panels use liquid crystals to control light.

questions.text: What is the full form of LED?
questions.explanation: LED: Light Emitting Diode. LEDs emit light when driven by electric current.

questions.text: What is the full form of CRT?
questions.explanation: CRT: Cathode Ray Tube. A CRT is a display tube used in older monitors.

questions.text: What is the full form of DPI?
questions.explanation: DPI: Dots Per Inch. DPI describes dot density in printing and related imaging contexts.

questions.text: What is the full form of USB?
questions.explanation: USB: Universal Serial Bus. USB connects peripherals and carries data and power.

questions.text: What is the full form of CD-ROM?
questions.explanation: CD-ROM: Compact Disc Read Only Memory. A CD-ROM is read-only optical storage.

questions.text: What is the full form of CD-RW?
questions.explanation: CD-RW: Compact Disc ReWritable. RW means rewritable; the disc can be erased and written again.

questions.text: What is the full form of DVD?
questions.explanation: DVD: Digital Versatile Disc. Digital Versatile Disc is the conventional expansion used here; some historical literature also uses Digital Video Disc, which is not a distractor.

questions.text: What is the full form of BD when referring to optical storage media?
questions.explanation: BD: Blu-ray Disc. BD names Blu-ray optical media.

references.locator: Question ID 324280 — BD in computer knowledge

questions.text: What is the full form of OS?
questions.explanation: OS: Operating System. The OS manages hardware resources and provides services to applications.

questions.text: What is the full form of DOS?
questions.explanation: DOS: Disk Operating System. DOS is a family of disk-oriented operating systems.

questions.text: What is the full form of GUI?
questions.explanation: GUI: Graphical User Interface. A GUI uses visual controls such as windows, icons and menus.

questions.text: What is the full form of CLI?
questions.explanation: CLI: Command Line Interface. A CLI accepts commands entered as text.

questions.text: What is the full form of ASCII?
options: American System Code for Internet Integration
American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Automatic Standard Code for Information Input
Advanced Symbol Code for Internal Interchange
questions.explanation: ASCII: American Standard Code for Information Interchange. ASCII defines codes for characters; standard ASCII uses seven bits.

questions.text: What is the full form of EBCDIC?
options: Electronic Binary Code for Digital Internet Communication
Extended Bit Character Data Integration Code
Enhanced Binary Coded Data Instruction Code
Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
questions.explanation: EBCDIC: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code. EBCDIC is a character-encoding family associated with IBM systems.

questions.text: What is the full form of BCD?
questions.explanation: BCD: Binary Coded Decimal. BCD represents each decimal digit using a binary code.

questions.text: What is the full form of BASIC?
questions.explanation: BASIC: Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code. BASIC is a programming-language family developed for accessibility.

questions.text: What is the full form of COBOL?
questions.explanation: COBOL: Common Business Oriented Language. COBOL is a language associated with business data processing.

questions.text: What is the full form of FORTRAN?
questions.explanation: FORTRAN: Formula Translation. FORTRAN derives its name from formula translation and is associated with scientific computing.

questions.text: What is the full form of FIFO in queue processing?
questions.explanation: FIFO: First In First Out. A queue normally removes the item that was inserted first.

questions.text: What is the full form of LIFO in stack processing?
questions.explanation: LIFO: Last In First Out. A stack normally removes the most recently inserted item first.

questions.text: What is the full form of DBMS?
questions.explanation: DBMS: Database Management System. A DBMS provides facilities to store, organize and retrieve data.

questions.text: What is the full form of RDBMS?
questions.explanation: RDBMS: Relational Database Management System. An RDBMS uses the relational model.

questions.text: What is the full form of SQL?
questions.explanation: SQL: Structured Query Language. SQL defines and manipulates data in relational database systems.

questions.text: What is the full form of DDL?
questions.explanation: DDL: Data Definition Language. DDL commands define database structures, for example CREATE TABLE.

questions.text: What is the full form of DML?
questions.explanation: DML: Data Manipulation Language. DML commands manipulate stored data, for example INSERT and UPDATE.

questions.text: What is the full form of DCL?
questions.explanation: DCL: Data Control Language. DCL concerns database permissions, for example GRANT and REVOKE.

questions.text: What is the full form of TCL in SQL transaction commands?
questions.explanation: TCL: Transaction Control Language. In SQL, TCL controls transactions using commands such as COMMIT and ROLLBACK.

questions.text: What is the full form of ODBC?
questions.explanation: ODBC: Open Database Connectivity. ODBC is a standard interface for accessing database systems.

questions.text: What is the full form of PDF?
questions.explanation: PDF: Portable Document Format. PDF is a document format designed to preserve layout.

questions.text: What is the full form of RTF?
questions.explanation: RTF: Rich Text Format. RTF can represent formatted text for exchange between applications.

questions.text: What is the full form of LAN?
questions.explanation: LAN: Local Area Network. A LAN connects devices across a limited local area.

questions.text: What is the full form of WAN?
questions.explanation: WAN: Wide Area Network. A WAN connects networks over broader geographic distances.

questions.text: What is the full form of MAN?
questions.explanation: MAN: Metropolitan Area Network. A MAN is associated with metropolitan-scale networking.

questions.text: What is the full form of WLAN?
questions.explanation: WLAN: Wireless Local Area Network. A WLAN provides local networking using wireless links.

questions.text: What is the full form of NIC?
questions.explanation: NIC: Network Interface Card. A network adapter connects a computer to a network. NIC is also expanded as Network Interface Controller; this valid variant is not used as a distractor.

questions.text: What is the full form of IP?
questions.explanation: IP: Internet Protocol. IP provides addressing and packet delivery between networks.

questions.text: What is the full form of TCP?
questions.explanation: TCP: Transmission Control Protocol. TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte-stream service.

questions.text: What is the full form of UDP?
questions.explanation: UDP: User Datagram Protocol. UDP sends datagrams without TCP-style delivery guarantees.

questions.text: What is the full form of DNS?
questions.explanation: DNS: Domain Name System. DNS resolves names using a distributed naming system; the expansion is System, not Server.

questions.text: What is the full form of DHCP?
questions.explanation: DHCP: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. DHCP supplies network configuration to clients.

questions.text: What is the full form of MAC in Ethernet networking?
questions.explanation: MAC: Media Access Control. MAC is a data-link-layer term; do not confuse it with an IP address.

questions.text: What is the full form of ARP?
questions.explanation: ARP: Address Resolution Protocol. ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to link-layer addresses on a local network.

references.locator: Question ID 324267 — MAC address from IP address

questions.text: What is the full form of OSI?
questions.explanation: OSI: Open Systems Interconnection. The OSI reference model organizes networking into seven layers.

questions.text: What is the full form of FTP?
questions.explanation: FTP: File Transfer Protocol. FTP is a protocol for transferring files.

questions.text: What is the full form of HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol. HTTP supports exchange of web resources.

questions.text: What is the full form of HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure. HTTPS refers to HTTP over a secure channel, commonly TLS.

questions.text: What is the full form of URL?
questions.explanation: URL: Uniform Resource Locator. A URL identifies the location of a resource.

questions.text: What is the full form of WWW?
questions.explanation: WWW: World Wide Web. The Web is a system of linked resources accessed over the internet.

questions.text: What is the full form of SMTP?
questions.explanation: SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. SMTP is used to submit and relay email.

questions.text: What is the full form of POP3?
questions.explanation: POP3: Post Office Protocol version 3. POP3 is an email-retrieval protocol.

questions.text: What is the full form of IMAP?
questions.explanation: IMAP: Internet Message Access Protocol. IMAP accesses mailboxes on a mail server.

questions.text: What is the full form of ISP?
questions.explanation: ISP: Internet Service Provider. An ISP supplies internet connectivity or related services.

questions.text: What is the full form of ISDN?
questions.explanation: ISDN: Integrated Services Digital Network. ISDN is a digital telecommunications network technology.

questions.text: What is the full form of PPP?
questions.explanation: PPP: Point to Point Protocol. PPP carries network-layer data over point-to-point links.

questions.text: What is the full form of SNMP?
questions.explanation: SNMP: Simple Network Management Protocol. SNMP supports network-device management.

questions.text: What is the full form of HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML: Hypertext Markup Language. HTML describes the structure and meaning of web content.

questions.text: What is the full form of CSS?
questions.explanation: CSS: Cascading Style Sheets. CSS specifies the presentation of documents such as HTML pages.

questions.text: What is the full form of XML?
questions.explanation: XML: Extensible Markup Language. XML is a markup language for structured data.

questions.text: What is the full form of SSL?
questions.explanation: SSL: Secure Sockets Layer. SSL is an older security-protocol family superseded by TLS.

questions.text: What is the full form of TLS?
questions.explanation: TLS: Transport Layer Security. TLS secures communications over a network.

questions.text: What is the full form of VPN?
questions.explanation: VPN: Virtual Private Network. A VPN establishes a logical private network over another network.

questions.text: What is the full form of PNG?
questions.explanation: PNG: Portable Network Graphics. PNG is a lossless raster image format.

questions.text: What is the full form of JPEG?
questions.explanation: JPEG: Joint Photographic Experts Group. JPEG names the standards group and is associated with widely used photographic image compression.

questions.text: What is the full form of GIF?
questions.explanation: GIF: Graphics Interchange Format. GIF is an image format that supports indexed colour and animation.

questions.text: What is the full form of SVG?
questions.explanation: SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics. SVG represents vector graphics using XML.

questions.text: What is the full form of API?
questions.explanation: API: Application Programming Interface. An API defines how software components interact.
